subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should the remaining work be rescued from the open incremental-session-sync PR, replaced with a fresh current-main design, or intentionally deferred in favor of the existing full-entry reindex behavior?
rationale: The source-visible problem remains, but the repair crosses stored memory metadata, batching semantics, transcript compaction, and session-state correctness, so the implementation direction needs maintainer ownership before another automated fix lane starts.

options.title: Fresh current-main design
options.body: Implement incremental session indexing against the current `memory_index_*` schema and batching paths with focused upgrade and compaction coverage.

options.title: Rescue the open PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or an owner to rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 and replace obsolete assumptions before review continues.

options.title: Defer incremental indexing
options.body: Keep full-entry reindexing if maintainers decide correctness simplicity is worth the long-session indexing cost for now.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main design
recommendation.body: Implement incremental session indexing against the current `memory_index_*` schema and batching paths with focused upgrade and compaction coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history points to this person for the memory engine and memory-host ownership boundary that the design must change.
